title: Flask Quiz
description: Review the 12 starter lessons. The questions name the example to revisit. Take your time, use the lessons, and read the reason after each answer.

questions.question: A route decorator connects GET / to a function. Its return value becomes the reply. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The decorator registers the function under /. Returning text lets Flask build the response. Keep the decorator directly above the function it belongs to.

questions.question: jsonify turns data into a JSON response. Open GET /book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: jsonify serialises both fields. Flask commonly sorts JSON object keys, which does not change their meaning. JSON field order is not meaningful; Flask may sort keys.

questions.question: Angle brackets mark a path input. GET /hello/Ravi passes Ravi to the function. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The path placeholder becomes the Python name input. Ravi is inserted into the greeting. A path value is untrusted input; do not paste it into raw HTML.

questions.question: The int converter accepts a whole-number path value. Open GET /double/4. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The int converter accepts 4 and gives the view an integer. The result is 8. A route converter decides whether the route matches before the function runs.

questions.question: request.args reads query-string values. Open GET /search?q=cat. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: request.args.get reads q and finds cat. The returned dictionary names it term. Query values are text unless you convert them.

questions.question: Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}. The code checks that the body is an object with text title. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: get_json reads the object. Its title is a string, so the created response branch is selected. Check parsed data before indexing into it.

questions.question: Returning a response with 404 tells the client that this book was not found. Open GET /missing. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The response tuple contains JSON plus status 404. Both pieces are sent together. A failure should not pretend to be a successful 200 response.

questions.question: url_for builds a URL from a function endpoint name. GET /start redirects a browser to /hello. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: url_for finds the hello endpoint. The redirect tells the browser to request that URL. The endpoint name here is the Python function name, not the URL text.

questions.question: make_response lets you add metadata before sending a reply. GET /note has Cache-Control: no-store. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: make_response builds a response first, allowing the cache header to be added before return. Headers describe the response; changing one does not change its body.

questions.question: before_request runs before route handlers. This practice check rejects paths under /closed. Visit GET /closed/books. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The hook sees the /closed/ prefix and returns a response. The later view is not called. Returning a response stops the request from reaching its view.

questions.question: An error handler formats a known error. GET /missing uses abort to raise a 404. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: abort raises a 404 HTTP error. The registered handler replaces its body while keeping 404. Keep the error status when returning a friendly error body.

questions.question: The test client calls the app without an open port. This example prints the returned JSON score. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The test client executes the view in memory. get_json reads score 8 from its response. Use the test client only for tests; it is not a public server.
